dumbbell-biceps-curl.description: A standing curl that trains both biceps through a palms-up arm path.
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms forward and elbows close to your sides.
Curl both dumbbells toward your shoulders without letting your upper arms drift forward.
Pause at the top, then lower the dumbbells under control until your arms are straight.
Keep your wrists stacked and torso still rather than using momentum to lift.

alternating-dumbbell-curl.description: A dumbbell curl performed one side at a time to focus on each arm independently.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides and palms facing forward.
Curl one dumbbell toward its shoulder while the opposite arm remains long and quiet.
Lower the working dumbbell smoothly, then repeat the same path with the other arm.
Keep both elbows beside your ribs and avoid leaning toward the working side.

seated-dumbbell-curl.description: A seated palms-up curl that limits lower-body assistance and isolates the biceps.
instructions: Sit upright against a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms forward and arms hanging down.
Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders while keeping your upper arms beside your torso.
Squeeze briefly, then lower both dumbbells with control to the hanging start position.
Keep your back against the bench and do not drive your shoulders forward.

barbell-biceps-curl.description: A two-arm barbell curl that builds the biceps with a fixed palms-up grip.
instructions: Stand tall holding the barbell with an underhand grip and your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Bend your elbows to curl the bar toward your upper chest while your upper arms stay still.
Pause before the bar reaches your shoulders, then lower it smoothly to straight arms.
Brace your trunk and avoid swinging your hips or bending your wrists.

ez-bar-curl.description: A curl using the angled grips of an EZ bar for a semi-supinated hand position.
instructions: Stand holding the inner angled grips of the EZ bar with your palms turned up and slightly inward.
Curl the bar toward your chest by bending your elbows without lifting your shoulders.
Hold the top position briefly, then lower the bar under control until your elbows open fully.
Keep your knuckles aligned with your forearms and your torso upright throughout.

hammer-curl.description: A neutral-grip dumbbell curl that emphasizes the elbow flexors and forearms.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs and thumbs pointing forward.
Curl both dumbbells upward while maintaining the neutral grip from bottom to top.
Pause near the shoulders, then lower the dumbbells slowly back beside your thighs.
Keep your elbows pinned near your ribs and avoid rotating or bending your wrists.

cross-body-hammer-curl.description: A neutral-grip curl that travels diagonally across the torso toward the opposite shoulder.
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, palms facing inward and shoulders level.
Curl one dumbbell diagonally across your torso toward the opposite shoulder without twisting it.
Lower it along the same diagonal path, then complete the movement with the other arm.
Keep your chest square and resist leaning or rotating as each dumbbell rises.

incline-dumbbell-curl.description: A curl from an inclined bench that begins with the upper arms slightly behind the torso.
instructions: Sit against an incline bench with dumbbells hanging below your shoulders and palms facing forward.
Curl the dumbbells upward while keeping your upper arms behind or in line with your torso.
Squeeze at the top, then slowly extend your elbows until the dumbbells hang beneath you again.
Keep your shoulders against the bench and do not swing the weights out in front.

concentration-curl.description: A supported single-arm curl that isolates the biceps from a seated position.
instructions: Sit with your feet apart and brace the back of one upper arm against the inside of the same-side thigh.
Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder while keeping the braced upper arm fixed.
Pause at the top, then lower the dumbbell slowly until the elbow is straight before switching sides.
Keep your wrist neutral and avoid pressing the elbow point into your thigh.

preacher-curl.description: A barbell curl with the upper arms supported on a preacher pad for a strict arm path.
instructions: Sit at the preacher bench with both upper arms flat on the pad and hold the barbell underhand.
Curl the bar toward your shoulders while maintaining contact between your upper arms and the pad.
Pause near the top, then lower the bar steadily until your elbows are nearly straight.
Keep your chest against the bench and avoid dropping into the bottom position.

dumbbell-preacher-curl.description: A single-arm dumbbell curl using a preacher pad to stabilize the upper arm.
instructions: Place one upper arm fully on the preacher pad and hold a dumbbell with your palm facing up.
Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder without lifting your arm away from the pad.
Squeeze briefly, then lower the dumbbell under control until the elbow is nearly straight before changing arms.
Keep your shoulder centered behind the working arm and do not bounce at the bottom.

cable-biceps-curl.description: A standing curl that uses a low cable to keep tension on the biceps throughout the motion.
instructions: Face a low cable and hold the bar attachment underhand with your elbows close to your sides.
Curl the bar toward your chest while keeping your shoulders down and upper arms still.
Pause at the top, then guide the bar back down until your arms are straight.
Stand far enough from the stack to keep the cable clear, and do not let it pull your torso forward.

single-arm-cable-curl.description: A unilateral low-cable curl that lets each biceps work through a consistent line of resistance.
instructions: Face a low pulley and hold its handle in one hand with your palm up and arm extended.
Curl the handle toward the same-side shoulder while keeping your elbow beside your ribs.
Pause at the top, then extend the arm slowly to the start position before switching sides.
Keep your hips and shoulders square so the cable does not rotate your body.

rope-hammer-curl.description: A cable curl with a rope attachment that maintains a neutral grip and steady tension.
instructions: Face a low cable, grasp the rope ends with palms facing each other, and stand with arms extended.
Curl the rope upward while keeping the ends separated and your upper arms close to your torso.
Squeeze near the top, then lower the rope smoothly until your elbows are straight.
Keep your wrists neutral and avoid pulling the rope apart with your shoulders.

high-cable-curl.description: A cable curl performed with the upper arms raised out to the sides for a shortened biceps position.
instructions: Stand centered between high pulleys and hold the handles with palms up and arms extended to the sides.
Curl the handles toward your temples while keeping your upper arms level and stationary.
Pause with your hands near your head, then straighten your elbows slowly to the wide start position.
Keep your ribs down and do not let the cables pull your shoulders forward.

machine-biceps-curl.description: A guided curl that supports the upper arms and keeps the biceps on a fixed path.
instructions: Adjust the seat so your elbows align with the machine pivot, then place your upper arms on the pad and grip the handles.
Curl the handles toward you while keeping your upper arms firmly supported.
Pause at the top, then lower the handles with control until your arms are nearly straight.
Keep your shoulders down and do not lift your elbows from the pad.

dumbbell-wrist-curl.description: A palms-up wrist curl that trains the forearm flexors with the forearms supported.
instructions: Sit with your forearms resting on your thighs or a bench, palms up and wrists extending beyond the edge.
Curl the dumbbells upward by flexing only your wrists while your forearms remain planted.
Pause at the top, then lower the dumbbells slowly until your wrists extend below the support.
Keep your hands aligned with your forearms and avoid lifting your elbows.

dumbbell-reverse-wrist-curl.description: A palms-down wrist curl that targets the forearm extensors with independent dumbbells.
instructions: Sit with your forearms supported, palms down and hands holding dumbbells beyond the edge of your thighs or bench.
Raise the backs of your hands by extending your wrists without moving your forearms.
Pause at the top, then lower the dumbbells under control until your wrists flex below the support.
Keep your grip secure and use only wrist motion rather than lifting your elbows.

barbell-wrist-curl.description: A two-handed palms-up wrist curl that works the forearm flexors in unison.
instructions: Sit with your forearms supported and hold a barbell underhand, wrists just beyond the edge of your thighs or bench.
Curl the bar upward by flexing both wrists while keeping your forearms still.
Pause at the top, then lower the bar smoothly until your wrists extend below the support.
Keep both hands level and maintain a closed grip around the bar.

barbell-reverse-wrist-curl.description: A two-handed palms-down wrist curl that emphasizes the forearm extensors.
instructions: Sit with your forearms supported and hold a barbell overhand, wrists extending beyond the edge.
Lift the back of both hands by extending your wrists while the forearms stay planted.
Pause at the top, then lower the bar slowly until your wrists flex toward the floor.
Keep the bar level and avoid opening your fingers or raising your elbows.

reverse-barbell-curl.description: An overhand barbell curl that shifts emphasis toward the forearms and brachialis.
instructions: Stand tall holding a barbell with a shoulder-width overhand grip and arms extended.
Curl the bar toward your chest while keeping your palms down and upper arms still.
Pause near the top, then lower the bar under control until your elbows are straight.
Keep your wrists in line with your forearms and avoid swinging your torso.

reverse-dumbbell-curl.description: An overhand dumbbell curl that trains each forearm while the elbows flex together.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing behind you and arms hanging at your sides.
Curl both dumbbells upward while maintaining the palms-down grip and steady upper arms.
Pause at the top, then lower the dumbbells smoothly to the start position.
Keep your wrists straight and do not flare your elbows or lean backward.

dead-hang.description: A stationary hang from a pull-up bar that develops grip endurance and overhead control.
instructions: Grip a secure pull-up bar overhand and move your feet clear so your arms support your body.
Hang with long arms, a steady trunk, and your shoulders held in a controlled position.
Finish by placing your feet back on the floor before releasing the bar.
Keep your grip fully closed and avoid swinging, twisting, or dropping from the bar.

plate-pinch-hold.description: A static grip exercise that challenges the fingers and thumbs by pinching a weight plate.
instructions: Stand tall and pinch the edge of a weight plate between your thumb and fingers with your arm at your side.
Hold the plate still with your wrist neutral and your shoulder level.
Finish by bending your knees and placing the plate securely on the floor before releasing it.
Keep your fingers clear of the underside and do not rest the plate against your leg.
